  <p class="vh-between">Between the first and second days there are seven weeks: time to submit the problem brief, read the pages of Classes 2 to 5 at your own pace, and finish the setup. The <a href="sessions.html">schedule</a> gives every block, break and due date.</p>

<section class="vh-section" aria-labelledby="vh-before">
  <h2 id="vh-before">Before Sunday 29 November</h2>
  <ul class="vc-checklist" id="before-day-1">
    <li>Bring a laptop on which you can install programs, and its charger.</li>
    <li>Create a GitHub account with a personal email you will keep after the course.</li>
    <li>Read the <a href="class1.html">Class 1 page</a>, about 90 minutes.</li>
    <li>Bring one problem from your organization in which people enter, read or act on information by hand.</li>
    <li>Watch for your instructor's email confirming the AI assistant and app builder for the course. If it has not arrived, come anyway: the remaining accounts are created in the room during the setup clinic.</li>
  </ul>
</section>

<section class="vh-section" aria-labelledby="vh-what">
  <h2 id="vh-what">What you build, and what you leave with</h2>
  <p class="vh-para">Each team takes one real problem from a member's organization to a deployed web application with an AI capability, then governs it and presents it to a panel. Along the way you use the building blocks of current AI work.</p>
  <dl class="vh-blocks-def">
    <div><dt>Web pages and apps</dt><dd>A deployed application with login and stored data, and a public page that explains it.</dd></div>
    <div><dt>Skills</dt><dd>"How we do it here", packaged so the assistant repeats it.</dd></div>
    <div><dt>Connectors and MCP</dt><dd>Scoped access to company systems, read before write.</dd></div>
    <div><dt>Agents</dt><dd>A model that takes steps with tools and waits for your approval.</dd></div>
    <div><dt>Automations</dt><dd>Work that starts on a schedule, with an owner and a log.</dd></div>
    <div><dt>Presentations</dt><dd>A Demo Day deck generated from your evidence and checked by you.</dd></div>
  </dl>
  <p class="vh-para">No programming experience is required or assumed. You leave with a working product, a test set and a risk memo for it, a small personal system for working with AI, and a tested way to decide between keeping a prototype, handing it to engineering, buying a product, or stopping.</p>
</section>

  <h2 id="vh-grade">Assessment</h2>
  <table class="vh-table">
    <thead><tr><th>Component</th><th>Who</th><th>Due</th><th>Weight</th></tr></thead>

      <tr><td>Demo Day</td><td>Team, individually adjusted</td><td>Sunday 17 January 2027</td><td>25%</td></tr>
      <tr><td>M3. AI feature, test set, agent and automation, risk memo</td><td>Team</td><td>Sunday 24 January 2027</td><td>25%</td></tr>
      <tr><td>Reflection memo and participation</td><td>Individual</td><td>Sunday 24 January 2027</td><td>15%</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
  <p class="vh-note">Written work is due at 23:59 on the day shown; Demo Day happens in the room. Everything is graded with one <a href="rubric.html">rubric</a>. The course is passed with 55 out of 100. Using AI is required and must be declared.</p>
</section>

<section class="vh-section" aria-labelledby="vh-data">
  <h2 id="vh-data">One rule from the first minute</h2>
  <p class="vh-para">Until your team has completed the Class 4 lab, closed every critical finding, and has the written agreement of the organization that owns the data, use only invented or de-identified information: no real names, phone numbers, addresses or tax numbers. Most teams will stay with de-identified data through Demo Day, and that costs nothing in the grade.</p>
</section>
